But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old techie fell into a trap by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal's combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Crafts, conversations & cultures converge at BRICS Bazaar
Article Text:
The bazaar was open to the public for free on 14-15 Sept

Patterns of unity at the entrance of the exhibition displayed patterns from 21 countries became a selfie spot

Craft, caught in the making

Lac bangles demonstration (L), a customised watch with clay pots (R )

Crossing borders, bridging cultures through craft

Cuban contemporary art (L) and papier-mache canvas (R )

‘Liked the diversity of handicrafts here’

Ethiopian coffee served live at the country's stall (L), Malaysian batik art (R )

Iran's rashti and balochi embroidery were a hit at the bazaar (L), Belarus' straw woven hats (R )

South African beadwork (L), Russian Ghzel pottery (R )

Kashmiri papier-mache is known for its intricate hand-painted designs





Against the backdrop of soft Indian instrumental music, the National Crafts Museum became a showcase of cultures from across the BRICS nations as the BRICS Bazaar brought together handicrafts, traditional art and artisans from participating countries. Hosted by the Ministry of External Affairs and the Ministry of Textiles, the exhibition drew visitors who explored crafts, interacted with artisans and experienced a slice of international culture in the city before concluding on Tuesday.A highlight of the exhibition was the craft demonstrations, including lac bangles, traditional pottery and papier-mâché painting. Lac bangles are an ancient art practised in Rajasthan. Shadab Ahmed, a ninth-generation artisan who has been making these bangles for over 30 years, made them live to order during the demonstrations. Karan Singh, a terracotta potter from Rajasthan tells us, “The size of the smallest pot here is 3mm. They’re also used to customise the watches where we remove the mechanism of the watch and place handmade pots inside.” Kashmiri papier-mâché is synonymous with Srinagar, where boxes, plates and pots adorned with detailed floral patterns are sold as souvenirs.Artisan Riyaz Ahmad shares that some intricate designs are painted with a brush as thin as a strand of hair.At the BRICS Bazaar, showcasing crafts and cultures from participating nations, a lively exchange unfolded as attendees browsed the stalls and interacted with artisans, using AI translation, gestures and handwritten notes to bridge the language gap. While Ethiopia served coffee with music, Iran introduced attendees to its embroidery traditions. India showcased Manipuri and Kashmiri handlooms, along with Mysore rosewood inlay and portrait weaving. Among the exhibitors was Vietnamese lacquer artist and university professor Tran Anh Tuan, who showcased paintings, vases, bowls and jewellery. He said, “I really like being here, the people are very friendly. I love Indian food, especially the curries!”Cuban artist Filiberto Mora Rosales, who has worked with papiermâché for over 40 years, said, “Being here is a magnificent experience. I sold out all the 30 items that I brought. Meeting artists from other countries is a very good experience.”Appreciating the exhibition, first-year student Prashasti from Lucknow, who recently moved to Delhi, said, “I’m so happy to be in Delhi because we are able to experience international cultures. I particularly liked the Russian and Chinese artwork here. The artisans are really enthusiastic. I think younger people are leading with pictures and then moving to the art, but older people are absorbing the art more.”Another attendee, Keith Jackson from Manipur, shared, “It’s a wonderful experience learning about so many different weavings and embroideries. I learnt that Iranian and Kashmiri embroidery are only slightly different. I liked the diversity of handicrafts here and bought a lot of stuff!”
Article Summary: The BRICS Bazaar brought together handicrafts, traditional art and artisans from participating countries. A highlight of the exhibition was the craft demonstrations, including lac bangles, traditional pottery and papier-mâché painting. The bazaar was open to the public for free on 14-15 Sept.

Article Title: ‘Rise in women’s participation encouraging’: CM unveils half marathon medal
Article Text:
Chief minister Rekha Gupta unveiled the finisher’s medal for the 21st edition of the Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon on Wednesday, ahead of the race scheduled for Oct 18

New Delhi:





Chief minister Rekha Gupta Wednesday unveiled the finisher’s medal for the 21st edition of Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon (VDHM), ahead of the race scheduled for Oct 18, and said sporting events of this scale could play an important role in promoting fitness, inclusion and greater public participation.Gupta said initiatives such as VDHM were aligned with the larger objectives of Fit India movement by encouraging people across age groups to take up physical activity. “When we talk about Fit India, these initiatives are important. The increase in participation of women is encouraging,” she said.Recalling her visit to the race last year, Gupta said she had initially planned to spend only a short time, but ended up staying longer after seeing the enthusiasm and energy among participants.CM also highlighted the participation of persons with disabilities, saying the event provided a platform for people from different backgrounds and abilities to come together. She also referred to the social causes associated with the race and stressed the importance of extending support to those in need. “Charity begins at home. We want to help those in need in whatever way possible.”Gupta added that Delhi govt would work with various stakeholders associated with VDHM to support its smooth conduct and make the upcoming edition a successful event.Now in its 21st edition, the half marathon has become a fixture on Delhi’s annual sporting calendar. Tourism minister Kapil Mishra said large sporting events “add to the branding and tourism of the city when they become part of the annual calendar”.The finisher’s medal has been crafted from pure zinc sourced from Hindustan Zinc’s Zawar mines in Udaipur. According to the organisers, its new design symbolises endurance and strength, with every runner completing the race receiving one. World Athletics Gold Label race will be flagged off from Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on Oct 18, with thousands of runners from India and abroad expected to participate.Priya Agarwal Hebbar, chairperson of Hindustan Zinc Ltd and non-executive director of Vedanta Ltd, said the event was also tied to #RunForZeroHunger campaign, under which participation supports efforts to provide food to children and animals in need. “Every kilometre run carries an inspiring purpose,” she said.Shreepad Shende, chief marketing officer of IDFC FIRST Bank, said the half marathon had grown over the years beyond being just a sporting event. He described it as “a movement that celebrates fitness, resilience and collective wellbeing”.Vivek Singh, joint managing director of Procam International, said organisers tried to ensure that the finisher’s medal carried a larger meaning for participants and served as a lasting reminder of the race. “Every year, we strive to create a medal that carries meaning and becomes a cherished memory for every runner,” he said.
Article Summary: Chief minister Rekha Gupta Wednesday unveiled the finisher’s medal for the 21st edition of Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon (VDHM) She said sporting events of this scale could play an important role in promoting fitness, inclusion and greater public participation. VDHM is aligned with the larger objectives of Fit India movement.

Article Title: LPG leak triggers blast at Sanpada snacks shop in Navi Mumbai, 2 injured
Article Text:
A LPG cylinder leakage caused a blast at a Sanpada snacks shop on Tuesday morning.





NAVI MUMBAI: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in sector-1, Sanpada on Tuesday morning. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.Purushottam Jadhav, Divisional officer of Vashi fire station said, "At 6.13 am, the Vashi fire station received the emergency call informing about a cylinder blast at a snacks shop in Pratik CHS on sector-1, Sanpada. The fire bridge team reached the spot within 5 minutes.It was found that the blast was due to leakage in one of the three LPG cylinders kept at snacks shop. The two men working at the snacks shop sustained severe burn injuries and were rushed to NMMC hospital, Vashi. Those injured were identified as Arjun Yadav (46) who has sustained 75 precent burn injuries and Manish Yadav (26), who has sustained 90 percent burns.The blast even caused damage to two shops adjacent to the snacks shop and three other shops in the neighbouring Abhimanyu CHS. While, the glass facade of Suraj hospital located opposite to Pratik CHS was shattered due to the impact of the blast."
Article Summary: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in Sanpada. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.

Article Title: Khalapur temple theft: Video shows masked man stealing silver Padukas; 2 arrested in Pune
Article Text:
he accused stole silver Charan Paduka from Shree Swami Samarth temple on September 2





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khalapur police probing the theft case wherein a masked man had decamped with a pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city on September 2, have arrested the acccused thief and his aide by tracking them to Pune on Monday.Pradeep Rayannavar, senior inspector of Khalapur informed that, the arrested accused are Mahendrasingh Rathod, 45, who hails from Rajasthan and Ravi Soni, 32, who hails from UP and is a history-sheeter as a theft case is registered against him in Pune.Both were presently residing in Chikhali, Pune district.On September 2, the temple trustee Deepak Bodarde, 68, lodged a complaint of theft of silver Padukas from the temple.When the CCTV footage of the temple premises was checked, it was seen that a masked man wearing a hat and attired in white Kurta-Payjama entering the temple around 7.30am.He goes to the first floor of the temple where the silver Padukas were kept in front of the idol of Shree Swami Samarth.By pretending to offer prayers, he picked up the Padukas and hid them inside his Kurta and exited the temple.Inspector Rayannavar said," The theft was committed when the temple priest had gone to his room near the temple.Upon checking the CCTV footage of the roads near the temple, it was seen that two masked men on a bike were loitering near the temple and conducted a reece before committing the theft.""Considering the religious sentiments of the devotees, Raigad SP forms a special police team to detect the case at the earliest. Subsequently, the CCTV footage along the escape route of the thieves were scanned. The bike used in the crime did not have a registration number plate," Rayannavar added.He further said, "However, using technical expertise, intelligence inputs and footages of CCTV camera along the highways, the thieves on bike were tracked and apprehended from Chikhali in Pune district. We have seized from them the stolen Padukas and the bike used in the crime. On Monday, the acccused were produced before the Khalapur JMFC court that remanded them to police custody till Friday."
Article Summary: A pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city were stolen on September 2. The accused thief and his aide were arrested by tracking them to Pune on Monday.

Article Title: Cop dies by suicide at Navi Mumbai lodge, names ex-DCP, ACP and head clerk in note alleging harassment
Article Text:
The deceased identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli, had recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media.In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.ASI Patil also left behind a nine-page suicide note accusing former DCP (Headquarters) Sanjay Patil, ACP Girish Thakare, and administrative head clerk Jayu Ahire of driving him to take the extreme step by allegedly harassing him while assigning official duties.ACP (Rabale Division) Rahul Dhas said, "ASI Patil had checked into Sachi Lodging and Boarding on Saturday at 4.40 pm. Around 7.30 pm, when the housekeeping staff went to his room, he did not respond, and the door was locked from inside. The lodge manager opened the door with a master key and found ASI Patil hanging from a ceiling fan hook. The lodge manager informed the Rabale MIDC police. ASI Patil was rushed to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead. Prima facie, an accidental death case will be registered at the Rabale MIDC police station."
Article Summary: Pandurang Nimba Patil, a 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police, allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening. He recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media. In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.

Article Title: 12-year-old girl, young woman rescued from prostitution racket in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Cops can be seen walking with 2 women. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose)





NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued a 12-year-old girl and a 26-year-old woman from a prostitution racket being carried out at a lodge in Nerul after conducting a raid by sending a decoy customer on Thursday.The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers by providing them rooms at Kohinoor Palace Lodging and Boarding in Shiravane village, Nerul.Gajanan Kadam, AHTU senior inspector, said the rescued minor girl hails from UP and resided in Shiravane village with her cousins, who had brought her from UP after telling her parents that she would be given a job.The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours after booking a room. The accused demanded Rs 4,000 for supplying a woman.After the accused accepted the amount, the decoy customer signalled the police team waiting outside the lodge, following which they raided the premises.Inspector Kadam said, “The arrested accused are the lodge managers identified as Hridaykumar Singh and Deepak Ramrakhiani and the waiter Kuleshwar Kumar Singh.”At Nerul police station, an FIR was registered against the arrested accused by invoking BNS sections for trafficking of persons and joint criminal liability, along with the POCSO Act, which defines punishment for abetment, such as helping, encouraging or plotting any sexual crime against a child, and the Prevention of Immoral Traffic Act.On Friday, the three accused were produced before the Belapur JMFC court, which remanded them to police custody till Sept 9.
Article Summary: The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers. The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours.

Article Title: Maharashtra horror: Teen murdered, body dumped near Mini Seashore
Article Text:
A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi





NAVI MUMBAI: A 19-year-old boy was murdered and his body was dumped on the pavement near a public garden along Mini Seashore Road in Sector 10A, Vashi, early on Saturday morning. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused.Shashikant Chandekar, senior inspector of Vashi police station, said, "The murder victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane. A passing pedestrian spotted him lying unconscious in a pool of blood on the pavement around 4am. The pedestrian alerted Vashi police station, and our police team reached the spot and took the teenager to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead due to severe blood loss from grievous injuries to his head and wrist after being assaulted with some sharp lethal weapon. The victim Mahato hails from Bihar and resided with his father, who is an auto-rickshaw driver, his mother and two minor siblings. He worked at a roadside Chinese food stall in Koparkhairane and used to drive his father's auto-rickshaw during the night."Inspector Chandekar added, "Mahato had left home on Friday around 9pm, telling his mother that he was going to work at the Chinese food stall and was taking his father's auto-rickshaw to ferry passengers throughout the night.After his body was found early on Saturday morning, his family was informed. His father's auto-rickshaw was not found at the crime scene. Hence, it is suspected that after fatally assaulting Mahato, the assailant took away the auto-rickshaw, which is being traced by scanning CCTV footage along the route from Koparkhairane to Vashi."As there is no CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we are scanning CCTV footage from roads leading to the crime spot where Mahato's body was dumped to zero in on the suspect. Mahato might have been fatally assaulted at the spot, or he might have been assaulted at another location and his body brought in a vehicle and dumped near Mini Seashore. Accordingly, using technical expertise, efforts are being made to detect the murder case. Meanwhile, Mahato's kin and friends are being questioned to get some lead on the unidentified accused."
Article Summary: A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused. The victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane.

Article Title: El Niño conditions linked to higher dengue risk in Kerala, IITM study finds
Article Text:
dengue Kerala

Pune:





El Niño-linked warming in Pacific Ocean could increase dengue risk in Kerala , a study led by Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune, has found as a powerful El Niño develops. The study, researchers said, could offer health authorities an early warning system months before the outbreaks.Kerala is currently experiencing a severe dengue season, recording 7,188 confirmed cases between June and Aug, around 60% above the decade-long average for the same period, data from the Kerala directorate of health services has revealed.Published in GeoHealth journal on Wednesday, the study analysed 14 years of dengue and climate data from Kerala (2006-2019) and found a clear link between El Niño years and higher dengue incidence. The researchers said warmer Pacific waters were associated with warmer and relatively drier pre-monsoon conditions in Kerala, creating favourable conditions for mosquito breeding before dengue cases surged during the monsoon.The study was led by Sophia Yacob and Dr Roxy Mathew Koll of IITM, in collaboration with ICMR’s National Institute of Translational Virology and AIDS Research (ICMR-NITVAR) and Savitribai Phule Pune University.“In our model-based analysis, Kerala’s high dengue years coincided with El Niño, while mild dengue years fell in La Niña years,” Dr Koll said.To convert this climate link into a forecasting tool, the team developed a machine-learning model that explained 72% of monthly variations in dengue cases in Kerala. The model suggested climate-driven dengue cases could increase 16-20% by 2040, and by up to 113% by the end of the century under a high-emissions scenario.The findings build on the team’s earlier Pune-focused research, which projected dengue risk in the city could rise 13-112% under warming scenarios. Dr Koll, however, said El Niño had a weaker influence on Pune than on Kerala. “We found that the role of El Niño in dengue risk over Pune is weak, while local weather conditions play a major role. In Pune, a combination of temperatures above 27°C, moderate and evenly distributed rainfall, and humidity between 60% and 78% during the monsoon (June-Sept) increases dengue incidence,” he said.A key finding was that Pacific sea-surface temperatures showed their strongest correlation with Kerala dengue cases about three months in advance. “When humidity and temperature patterns are included, the lead time extends to nearly five months, enough to allow authorities to strengthen mosquito-control measures and prepare hospitals ahead of seasonal spikes,” Yacob said.The researchers cautioned that the study period ended in 2019 and therefore could not directly attribute Kerala’s current dengue season to the ongoing El Niño event. Instead, it highlighted a historical pattern that mirrored present conditions.The study also stresses that climate was only one part of the dengue equation. Factors like vector control, water storage practices, waste management, urbanisation and disease surveillance continued to play a critical role in determining outbreak severity.“Climate signals can give us a head start by several months,” Dr Koll said, adding, “Combined with health and mosquito surveillance, they can help us intensify vector control, prepare hospitals and reach vulnerable communities before the seasonal surge.”Co-author Dr Sreelakshmi PR, scientist at ICMR-NITVAR, said the findings underscored the need to integrate climate indicators into routine dengue surveillance, rather than relying solely on case counts.
Article Summary: Kerala is currently experiencing a severe dengue season, recording 7,188 confirmed cases between June and Aug, around 60% above the decade-long average for the same period. The study could offer health authorities an early warning system months before the outbreaks.

Article Title: Journalist arrested over defamatory video against woman
Article Text:
In Custody

Chennai:





City police arrested Nakheeran reporter Damodaran Prakash, 58, on Wednesday following a complaint from a 38-year-old woman YouTube host over a video that contained derogatory remarks and personal allegations against her. Police said the video had been uploaded in Jan 2026.According to the complaint, the video used the woman’s photograph and made false claims about her personal life. Adambakkam police had registered a case for offences punishable under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act. A team led by the Adambakkam police inspector arrested Prakash at his residence in Chintadripet on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Nakheeran reporter Damodaran Prakash, 58, arrested following a complaint from a 38-year-old woman YouTube host. Police said the video had been uploaded in Jan 2026. Adambakkam police had registered a case for offences punishable under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.
